Figure caption: Physicochemical characterization of mUox@iLAND and cellular entry.A Schematic representation of mUox@iLAND, B Hydrodynamic size, polydispersity index (PDI), zeta potential, and encapsulation efficiency of mUox@iLAND. C Transmission electronic microscope (TEM) was used to determine the rough morphology and size. D Records of hydrodynamic size and PDI at different storage time points. E pKa determination using TNS assay, the pKa recorded was 6.02. F Cellular uptake behavior of Cy5-NA@iLAND in comparison with Cy5-NA@Lipo2000 via confocal microscopy using Hepa1-6 cells. Scale bar, 40 µm. G–H Quantitative analysis of mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) (G) and co-localization of Cy5 signal and lysotracker signal (H) in (F). I Cellular uptake was also determined using FACS analysis using Hepa1-6 cells, and (J) the MFI was also analyzed. The results in (C, F) were representative of three independent experiments. Data in (B, D, E, G, H, J) were presented as mean ± SD, n = 3 biologically independent samples. Source data are provided as a Source Data file.

Figure caption: In vitro performances of iLAND.Comparison of intracellular trafficking, endosomal escape, and mechanism exploration of transfection of iLAND & Lipo2000. A Internalization of Cy5-NA@iLAND in Hepa1-6 cells after receiving various treatments including (G1) Mock, (G2) genistein and iLAND, (G3) Clorpromazine-HCl and iLAND, (G4) Amiloride-HCl and iLAND, (G5) iLAND. B Quantitative analysis of the MFI in (A). C In vitro Uox expression by mUox@Lipo2000 and mUox@iLAND. D Cell viability of Hepa1-6 after treatment with mUox@Lipo2000 and mUox@iLAND at different transfection concentrations. E Intracellular uptake at different time points. Scale bars, 40 µm. F, H Quantitative analysis of the MFI in (E). G, I Co-localization of Cy5 signal and lysotracker signal in (E). The smaller the Pearson’s correlation value, the less overlapped fluorescence signal, indicating higher endosomal escape efficiency. The results in (A, C, E) were representative of three independent experiments. Data were presented as mean ± SD, n = 3 biologically independent samples in (B, F–I) and n = 6 biologically independent samples in (D). Source data are provided as a Source Data file.

Figure caption: In vivo biodistribution and mRNA expression of Cy5-NA@iLAND.Cy5-NA@MC3 and Cy5-NA@SM-102 were introduced as controls. All LNPs were injected at 0.5 mg/kg with Cy5-NA intravenously. A Fluorescence imaging of the whole body at 1, 3, 6, 24 and 48 h and isolated organs at 3, 6, 24 and 48 h after administration. PBS, phosphate buffered saline; NA, nucleic acid; SmG, submandibular gland; T, thymus gland; H, heart; L, lung. B, C The MFI of Cy5 signal in the whole body (B) at 1, 3, 6, 24 and 48 h and isolated livers (C) at 3, 6, 24 and 48 h post-injection. D Bioluminescence imaging the whole body at 1, 3, 6, 24 and 48 h and isolated organs at 3, 6, 24 and 48 h after administration. E, F Quantifying luciferase expression in the whole body (E) and isolated livers (F) at different time points. Avg, average. Five animals were used in each group. G Confocal images of liver cryosections (4 µm) from mice receiving intravenous injections of PBS, Cy5-NA@MC3, Cy5-NA@SM-102 or Cy5-NA@iLAND, respectively. Asterisks mark representative hepatocytes, and arrows indicate representative nonparenchymal cells. Scale bars, 20 µm. Data in (A, B, D, E) were presented as mean ± SD, n = 5 biologically independent mice. The results in (G) were representative of three independent experiments. Source data are provided as a Source Data file.

Figure caption: In vivo efficacy study in a sustained hyperuricemia mouse model.A Schematic representation of treatment procedures and grouping information. B SUA level before and after hyperuricemia induction. C SUA levels in mice receiving various treatments including PBS, mUox@iLAND (single dose), and allopurinol (daily). Normal mice were used as control group. D Determination of body weight during the study. E–L Serum biochemistry parameters evaluation of various samples. AST, aspartate aminotransferase; ALT, alanine aminotransferase; TCHOL, total cholesterol; GLU, glucose; TRIG, triglyceride; HDL-C, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol; LDL-C, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Data in (B–L) were presented as mean ± SD, with n = 7 mice in G1, n = 8 mice in G2-G3 and n = 5 mice in G4. P value was calculated by one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with a Tukey post-hoc test. *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001. Source data are provided as a Source Data file.

Figure caption: In vivo anti-hyperuricemic evaluation in purine-rich food intake mouse model.A Schematic illustration of the treatment course and grouping information. B SUA levels before and after the disease model establishment. C SUA levels during the whole treatment course. D Body weight of the mice during the whole course. E–L Serum biochemistry parameters evaluation of various samples. AST, aspartate aminotransferase; ALT, alanine aminotransferase; GLU, glucose; TCHOL, total cholesterol; TRIG, triglyceride; HDL-C, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol; LDL-C, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Data in (B–L) were presented as mean ± SD, with n = 11 mice in G1, n = 8 mice in G2-G3 and n = 7 mice in G4. P value was calculated by one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with a Tukey post-hoc test. *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001. Source data are provided as a Source Data file.

Figure caption: Metabolomic analysis of liver tissues.A–C Differential metabolites were visualized in the form of volcanic map. Based on univariate analysis, volcano plots displayed differential changes of metabolites in positive channel. The red circles represented upregulation; the blue circles represent down-regulation. Fold change (FC) > 1.5 or FC < 0.67, p value < 0.05. D Heatmap shows primary metabolites involved in purine metabolism. Heatmap also compares various metabolites involved in the purine metabolism pathway. The consistency of important metabolites from the purine-degradation pathway is also analyzed. Data in (A–C) were presented as mean, n = 3 biologically independent samples. Student’s t-test is then used to determine the significance (p-value) of differences in metabolite expression between comparison groups. The Benjamini-Hochberg method corrects these p-values to obtain q-values, which are used to evaluate the significance of metabolite differences between the two sample groups. Data in (A–D) were presented as mean, n = 3 biologically independent samples. Source data are provided as a Source Data file.
